summary: The article argues that cybersecurity awareness and continuous training of financial-sector employees is essential as cyber-attacks grow more sophisticated and exploit human error. It follows a fictional-style day of bank teller Jordan Ellis at Midtown Federal to illustrate hands-on phishing training, weekly updates, and quarterly incident drills. Quotes from executives and experts stress that training must be ongoing, timely, and treated as a shared responsibility.
one_line: Financial institutions are investing in hands-on, continuous employee cybersecurity training, illustrated by teller Jordan Ellis at Midtown Federal, to counter human-error-driven attacks.
key_facts: On September 6, 2023, a leading multinational bank thwarted a potentially devastating ransomware attack, per the article.
A 2023 report by CyberTech International says banks and financial institutions increased spending on employee cybersecurity training by an average of 40% in the past year.
On March 12, 2023, a neighboring bank was breached when an employee inadvertently clicked a malicious link, giving hackers access to sensitive customer data.
Jordan Ellis is a bank teller at Midtown Federal, a mid-sized bank headquartered in New York City; she logs on at 8:45 a.m. and completes a mandatory phishing training module.

Midtown Federal's training was developed by Chief Information Security Officer Sophia Rodriguez, who joined on January 2, 2023, and includes interactive simulations of spear phishing and social engineering.

Jordan spotted a phishing email asking her to verify log-in details by noticing an unfamiliar sender's domain and an urgent tone, then reported it to the cybersecurity team, which confirmed it was phishing.
Thompson Clark, Midtown Federal's CEO, called the neighboring bank's breach 'a wake-up call for all of us in the industry' and said employee cybersecurity education 'is not optional'.
Andrew Peterson, a cybersecurity analyst at Midtown Federal, said the bank has moved past theory-based sessions to stress and decision-making scenarios resembling real attacks.

Midtown Federal employees receive weekly updates on new cyber threats, and every quarter all staff take part in a full-scale cyber incident drill covering breach containment and communication with regulators and customers.
Dr. David Kidman, a cybersecurity consultant, said at a security conference on October 15, 2023 that training is 'not a one-time affair but a career-long commitment'.

Todd Reynolds, a cybersecurity trainer, says training should be timely and draw on the latest incidents and threat intelligence; Midtown Federal incorporates recent internal and external incidents into its materials.

Training also covers cyber hygiene: managing passwords, securing personal devices used for work, and safely handling customer information; employees such as Jordan also advise clients on securing online banking accounts.
